text: A push to main whose tree a pull request's gate passed on doesn't run the checks and tests again (#874). It still verifies every project, gathers the receipts and reports invariant/gate, so each commit on main keeps its gate and its receipts, as D-0083 has it. A gate that passes on a pull request records the tree it tested, the pull request merged into its base, as an artifact named for the tree's hash and kept seven days, and the push's first job asks GitHub for it. Only a run of this workflow on a pull request from this repository that passed counts, so a fork's run doesn't, and whatever can't be asked or read runs everything. A pull request merged after main moved has a tree no gate saw, and so has a direct push: they run everything, which is what main's second run is for (#436). The trees #868's and #864's gates tested were the trees that landed, and main's run after each repeated about 185 of its 253 runner-minutes on them; with 20 runners, nine runs on 2026-11-12 took 49 to 126 minutes each, with jobs waiting up to 44 minutes for one.
